title: Boutique store demo: choose the look
question: The roll picked the Cash on Delivery Slip. Keep it, take another card, or re-roll.

options.label: Cash on Delivery Slip
options.lineage: the courier consignment note every Pakistani shopper signs at the door: a carbon copy slip, a barcode, the COD amount box, a city code and kraft parcel tape
options.thesis: The store as the parcel on its way to you: every piece wears a consignment label with its price in the COD amount box, its stitching spelled out and its delivery days by city, so ordering feels as certain as signing for the parcel.
options.viewport: This week's lawn suit as a big photo with a consignment label stuck on its corner: article code, 3-piece unstitched, Rs 6,490 in the COD amount box, Lahore 1 day and Karachi 3 days. The boutique's name sits stamped in the sender block, with an Add to parcel button.
options.risk: A courier slip is a logistics object. If the photos are small, it reads like a tracking site instead of a boutique.

raised.raise: One piece per view on the home page, with real empty space around it, so the clothes feel chosen, not stocked.
One accent colour is kept for one job only: the courier orange marks the thing you are about to pay for.
Order states print themselves as lines on the slip (packed, handed to courier, out for delivery) instead of badges.
Prices and quantities sit in tabular figures in ruled boxes, so totals line up like a real bill.
Buttons press down like a rubber stamp and leave a short mark, so every add to parcel feels done.
The new collection is ranked by weight: this week's drop is set biggest, and older drops step down in size.

options.label: Lawn Lookbook
options.lineage: the printed lawn brochure brands hand out before the summer launch: full bleed model shots, a swatch of each print, the article code and price on the facing page
options.thesis: The store as this season's lookbook: you turn pages of full bleed looks, each with its print swatch, code and price, and add to bag straight from the spread.
options.viewport: A full bleed model shot on the left page, the print swatch and article code with the price on the right, and a page number in the corner.
options.risk: The most familiar choice for a lawn brand. It can look like every designer's launch site.

options.label: Sound System Bill
options.lineage: a screened dance poster on fluorescent card, names ranked in outlined block caps
options.thesis: The collection as a sale bill: this week's drop in the biggest block caps, prices struck across like a venue line.
options.viewport: Ranked block caps of the new drops over fluorescent card, with the sale price struck across the middle.
options.case: Holds audience identification, because Pakistani lawn sale banners use the same loud fluorescent print, but the clothes lose to the type.
options.risk: Loud enough to bury the clothes.

options.label: Ikebana Alcove
options.lineage: one branch and three irises in a quiet alcove
options.thesis: One outfit at a time in charged empty space.
options.viewport: One suit off centre in a pale alcove.
options.case: Fuses poorly: too quiet and foreign for a Lahore boutique's customers.
options.kept: Empty space as the sign of care.

options.label: Film Bloom
options.lineage: hand processed 16mm film with light leaks
options.thesis: Looks as frames on a scratched strip.
options.viewport: A strip of outfit frames with one lit by an orange leak.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the grain and leaks fight the true colours of the fabric.
options.kept: One accent kept for one state.
options.risk: Colours of the clothes become untrustworthy.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.lineage: a green phosphor terminal at midnight
options.viewport: A green transcript listing the collection.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a terminal cannot show a print or a colour.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.lineage: a darkroom printer's exposure record with zone sheets
options.thesis: Products as hatched sheets on a zone ramp.
options.case: Fuses poorly: technical and cold for fashion.

options.label: Rubber Hose Cel
options.lineage: an early sound era cartoon cel framed by an iris
options.thesis: The store as a sequence of cartoon gags.
options.viewport: A product inside an oval iris with bouncy buttons.
options.case: Fuses poorly: black and white cartoons cannot carry fabric colour.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean white fashion store with big model photos, a filter bar and a quick add to bag, done very well.
canonCard.viewport: A full width campaign photo, then a grid of products with prices and a filter bar.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other Pakistani fashion brand's site.
